author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both the browser and machine-readable veterinarian directory surfaces accept an optional specialty filter, returning only veterinarians holding that whole specialty name matched case-insensitively; an unknown specialty yields an empty directory with success, a blank value acts as no filter, and browser paging carries the filter. No visible control is added in this request.
acceptance_criteria: The browser directory filtered by a held specialty lists only those veterinarians, still a page at a time.
The machine-readable directory filtered by a held specialty returns only those veterinarians.
A specialty value matches on the whole specialty name and is case-insensitive; a value that is only the start of a specialty name does not match.
A specialty that no veterinarian holds returns the surface's normal directory with an empty veterinarian list and a success outcome.
An empty or whitespace-only filter value behaves as though no filter were given; with no filter value both surfaces behave as they do today.
A filtered browser directory spanning more than one page keeps the same specialty filter when a paging link is followed.
Neither surface gains a visible specialty-picking control in this request.
non_goals: A visible specialty-picking control (form, dropdown, or other page element) on either surface in this request
notes: Fresh REQ; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. NG-9 narrowed 2026-08-07 (see adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-free-text-vet-search.md). Open question in prd.md: whether a non-blank filter value's surrounding whitespace is trimmed before matching — narrowest reading is a literal whole-name compare; no slice depends on it yet.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the existing paged veterinarian directory (VetController + cached VetRepository) with an optional specialty filter on both surfaces. Filtering is done in memory over the already-cached vet collection, not via a Spring Data query, because Vet.specialties is an EAGER @ManyToMany (a paged join cannot page at the DB) and the full collection is already cached by design. The whole-name, case-insensitive match is a domain predicate on the Vet aggregate, keeping the match out of the controller so the architecture-principles Web-controller row (no business rule in a controller) stays satisfied. Recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts note + adr/2026-08-07-vet-directory-filter-in-memory.md.
integration_points: Vet gains a whole-name case-insensitive specialty predicate (e.g. boolean hasSpecialty(String)) — new domain query on the aggregate, unit-testable without the web layer

VetController.showVetList(page, specialty): when specialty is null/blank keep today's DB-paged findAll(pageable); when present, read cached findAll(), filter by the Vet predicate, and wrap the requested page in a PageImpl so the existing addPaginationModel model attributes are unchanged
VetController.showResourcesVetList(specialty): when present, filter the cached findAll() collection and wrap in the existing Vets; the serialized surface stays unpaged, as today
VetController adds the filter value to the model so vetList.html pagination links carry it
vetList.html pagination anchors switch to the Thymeleaf param form so page and specialty travel together, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}
VetRepository requires no change — findAll (cached) is the filter's data source; the prd-entry listed it as a target but the in-memory design does not touch it

patterns.description: input normalization precedent: owner search treats a null/blank last name as the broadest search; the specialty filter mirrors this blank-is-no-filter handling at the controller boundary
existing in-memory query surface on the Vet aggregate (getSpecialties sorted, getNrOfSpecialties); the new hasSpecialty predicate extends the same read-only-over-own-state pattern
Design Validation Checklist: no business rule added to a web controller — the specialty match must live on Vet, not in VetController

risks.risk: Putting the case-insensitive whole-name match inside VetController would be a fresh Web-controller-row violation (architecture-principles is explicit the existing deviation does not extend to new rules)
risks.mitigation: Place the match on the Vet aggregate as a predicate; the controller only normalizes input, filters, paginates, and wraps — orchestration, not a rule

risks.risk: Non-blank value with incidental surrounding whitespace (e.g. ' surgery ') — the PRD leaves trimming open (Open Question) and no acceptance test covers it
risks.mitigation: Implement the narrowest reading: normalize only the blank case (isBlank -> no filter) and compare a non-blank value literally via equalsIgnoreCase without stripping; this decides nothing the open question reserves and passes every acceptance bullet. A visible-control follow-up settles it

risks.risk: A paged Spring Data query joining the EAGER specialties collection would trigger Hibernate in-memory pagination (HHH warning) and duplicate Vet roots without DISTINCT — the naive 'just add a repository method' fix reintroduces this
risks.mitigation: In-memory filter over the cached collection avoids the join-with-paging entirely; ADR records the departure so a reviewer does not 'correct' it back to a repository query

risks.risk: Thymeleaf may render specialty= (empty) on pagination links when no filter is active
risks.mitigation: Harmless: an empty/blank specialty is normalized to no filter by the controller, so the unfiltered paging behavior is unchanged

notes: REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn; this reinstates the /vets JSON surface as REQ-VET-003's first capability. Removed the now-stale 'machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement / pending removal' row from system-design.md Known Defects, since REQ-VET-003 gives that route a requirement. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Vets wrapper Implements deliberately left as '—' — the JSON surface's requirement is carried by VetController, not the container.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Reflected specialty parameter flows only into Thymeleaf @{...} link expressions, which URL-encode query values and HTML-escape attribute output; no th:text reflection of the value, so no reflected XSS.
Filtering is in-memory via Java equalsIgnoreCase over the cached collection with no query built from the parameter, so no SQL/injection sink.
JSON /vets surface does not echo the parameter into the response body; only matching Vet objects are serialized by Jackson, and the endpoint exposes only already-public directory data.
Untrusted input is normalized to null at the controller boundary before use.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: filterBySpecialty calls vetRepository.findAll() (the full-collection, cache-backed variant) rather than a specialty-parameterized repository query. This is the correct and intentional design — the EAGER @ManyToMany means a DB-paged join would trigger Hibernate in-memory pagination — but there is no why-comment at the call site. A future reader with no ADR context will treat this as an oversight and refactor it to a @Query method, reintroducing the HHH90003004 warning. The ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-07-vet-directory-filter-in-memory.md records the rationale; the code should point to it.
findings.fix: Add a single-line comment above the findAll() call inside filterBySpecialty: '// Full-collection fetch: cached by VetRepository; see docs/adr/2026-08-07-vet-directory-filter-in-memory.md for why a DB query is not used here.'

approved_aspects: Vet.hasSpecialty Javadoc accurately describes the whole-name, case-insensitive contract and is precise about what does not match (prefix-only values)
hasSpecialty uses getSpecialtiesInternal() rather than getSpecialties() — avoids creating a sorted defensive copy for a read that does not require order
normalizeSpecialty is a focused, well-commented private method that mirrors the OwnerController blank-is-no-filter precedent and uses isBlank() for Unicode-correct whitespace handling
findPaginated cleanly separates the two branches: DB-paged findAll(pageable) when unfiltered, in-memory PageImpl when filtered; the subList boundary guard (start >= filtered.size()) is correct
All five pagination link templates (numbered, first, prev, next, last) carry specialty=${specialty}, satisfying the filter-persistence acceptance criterion
No business rule logic was introduced into VetController — the case-insensitive match lives on the Vet aggregate where it belongs

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The PRD acceptance criterion 'given a specialty that no veterinarian holds, when either surface is filtered by it, then that surface returns successfully with an empty veterinarian list' covers both surfaces. unknownSpecialtyShouldReturnEmptyDirectoryWithSuccess tests only the HTML surface (GET /vets.html?specialty=nutrition). No test covers GET /vets?specialty=<unknown> returning HTTP 200 with an empty vetList on the JSON surface. A defect on the JSON empty-list path would be undetected.

The PRD acceptance criterion 'given a filter value that is empty or only spaces, when either surface is filtered by it, then the surface behaves as though no filter were given' covers both surfaces. blankSpecialtyValueShouldBehaveAsNoFilter tests only the HTML surface (GET /vets.html with param specialty='   '). No test covers GET /vets with a blank specialty parameter on the JSON surface.

filteredBrowserPaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyAcrossPages contains a for-loop constructing 7 radiologist vets. The testing brief requires test bodies to be straight-line code with no loops. Extract the list construction to a factory method such as radiologistsOf(int count) in the test class body, then call it from the test.
findings.fix: Extract the for-loop into a private List<Vet> radiologistsOf(int count) factory method and replace the loop with a single radiologistsOf(7) call.

findings.description: specialtyFilterShouldMatchWholeNameCaseInsensitively repeats three identical assertThat(vet.hasSpecialty(...)).isTrue() calls for 'radiology', 'Radiology', and 'RADIOLOGY'. The testing brief requires @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource for repetitive test cases. Converting this removes the duplication and makes it trivial to add further case variants.
findings.fix: Convert to @ParameterizedTest @MethodSource (or @CsvSource) supplying ["radiology", "Radiology", "RADIOLOGY"] as inputs, with a single assertThat(vet.hasSpecialty(input)).isTrue() assertion.

findings.description: All 8 test names declared in the prd-entry test_names field follow the pattern {Subject}Should{Outcome} but omit the 'the' prefix required by the brief's naming school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}). The implementer used the exact declared names, so this is a defect in the prd-entry. Future prd-entry records should declare test names with the 'the' prefix, e.g. theHtmlDirectoryShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty. Whether the current test method names should be renamed (decoupling from the prd-entry's declared names) needs a decision from the product-requirements-expert.

AssertJ fluent assertions used throughout VetTests.java unit tests
MockMvc is the only new mock introduced; @MockitoBean VetRepository is pre-existing tolerated infrastructure for the @WebMvcTest slice — no new internal code is mocked

author: product-requirements-expert
answer: Decision: rename all 8 test methods on this slice to add the 'the' prefix. Verified: docs/testing-principles.md line 86 defines the naming school as 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}' (prefix is load-bearing, per the theOwnerSearchShouldMatchOnLastNamePrefix example); line 96 scopes the school to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward, so these new tests (written this slice) are bound by it; scripts/layout.toml test_name_pattern '^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$' is only the looser machine floor (line 88) and does not enforce the prefix. The declared names omit it, so the prd-entry (line 2) was defective and the implementer correctly used the declared names. Rename is a pure identifier change, no behavior change, in scope for the slice that created these tests. Exact final names: (1) VetControllerTests: htmlDirectoryShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty -> theHtmlDirectoryShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty; (2) VetControllerTests: jsonDirectoryShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty -> theJsonDirectoryShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty; (3) VetTests: specialtyFilterShouldMatchWholeNameCaseInsensitively -> theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchWholeNameCaseInsensitively (keep this exact name when converting it to @ParameterizedTest per the separate autofix finding — parameterized tests keep one method name, testing-principles line 94); (4) VetTests: prefixSpecialtyValueShouldNotMatchAnyVet -> thePrefixSpecialtyValueShouldNotMatchAnyVet; (5) VetControllerTests: unknownSpecialtyShouldReturnEmptyDirectoryWithSuccess -> theUnknownSpecialtyShouldReturnEmptyDirectoryWithSuccess; (6) VetControllerTests: blankSpecialtyValueShouldBehaveAsNoFilter -> theBlankSpecialtyValueShouldBehaveAsNoFilter; (7) VetControllerTests: filteredBrowserPaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyAcrossPages -> theFilteredBrowserPaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyAcrossPages; (8) VetControllerTests: absentSpecialtyShouldListDirectoryAsToday -> theAbsentSpecialtyShouldListDirectoryAsToday. Scope limit: rename only these 8, prefix-only, change nothing else; do not touch the pre-existing suite (line 96 exempts it). The feature-implementer owns the test files and applies the renames. Going forward I will declare prd-entry test_names with the 'the' prefix; I am not superseding the line-2 prd-entry, since this response is the authoritative correction and a re-issue would risk re-triggering upstream stages.
notes: Resolves the clarify finding at line 14 (test-reviewer). Feature-implementer applies the renames; I did not edit test files.
